subject: Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia Community Forum
overview: Medical experts and community advocates gathered for a Black Health Series event focused on Alzheimer's disease, dementia diagnosis, disparities in health outcomes, and caregiver support. The panel detailed available clinical research opportunities, diagnostic testing methods, and practical strategies for memory health and care planning.

items.title: Interactive Warm-Up and Warning Signs Analogy
items.summary: Mike Kincaid led an interactive visual exercise illustrating how subtle warning signs of cognitive change can easily be missed.

items.title: Dementia Overview and Disparities in Alzheimer's Disease
items.summary: Mike Kincaid explained the differences between general dementia and Alzheimer's disease, highlighting reversible causes and statistical disparities affecting women, African Americans, and Hispanic populations.

items.title: Medical Research Ethics and Community Trust
items.summary: Presenters addressed participant questions about historical medical mistreatment, explaining modern institutional safety protocols and patient rights in clinical trials.

items.title: Patient Advocacy and Specialist Referrals
items.summary: Dr. Christine Ritchie and Mike Kincaid encouraged patients and families to advocate for themselves by seeking second opinions and requesting neurological diagnostic referrals.

items.title: Post-Diagnosis Legal and Care Planning
items.summary: The panel emphasized completing healthcare proxies, powers of attorney, and legal arrangements promptly following a dementia diagnosis.

items.title: Diagnostic Testing and Benefits of Clinical Research
items.summary: Dr. Christine Ritchie and Dr. Ramirez-Gomez explained diagnostic options, including PET scans and blood tests, and noted that research study participants receive comprehensive medical evaluations.

items.title: Caring for the Caregiver and Managing Dementia Symptoms
items.summary: Dr. Christine Ritchie presented strategies for caregiver self-care, symptom management, safety planning, driving transitions, and avoiding social isolation.

items.title: Research Opportunities: Social Study and Mind-Body Interventions
items.summary: Sahana, Dr. Ramirez-Gomez, and Dr. Tony Pham introduced research studies, including a virtual caregiver support program and a mind-body intervention for older Black Americans experiencing chronic pain and cognitive decline.

items.title: The AHEAD Study for Early Alzheimer's Detection
items.summary: Dr. Seth Gale presented virtually on the AHEAD study, which uses blood tests and PET scans to evaluate early interventions in adults aged 55 to 80 before memory symptoms appear.

items.title: Preventative Lifestyle Factors and Closing Remarks
items.summary: Dr. Seth Gale reviewed modifiable lifestyle factors such as aerobic exercise, diet, and treating hearing loss, before event organizer Sophie concluded the meeting with an announcement for an upcoming event on Black maternal health.
